review.diagnosis: Probable atrial-predominant inflammatory cardiomyopathy (atrial myocarditis), provisionally postinfectious, causing extensive atrial electrical failure and complete atrioventricular block.
review.reasoning: Worsening dyspnea and edema approximately two weeks after a respiratory illness, modest troponin elevation, and left atrial enhancement with borderline edema favor an inflammatory atrial process. Preserved LV systolic function and absence of substantial ventricular scar support atrial-predominant involvement. Confirmed findings include absent surface P waves, a narrow-QRS escape rhythm at 42/min, electrically silent right atrium with limited septal capture, complete AV block, and absent response to coronary-sinus pacing. These establish extensive atrial electrical dysfunction, but not its histologic cause. RV dilation/dysfunction, severe tricuspid regurgitation, and elevated estimated pulmonary pressure accompany congestive symptoms; their full relationship to the atrial disease remains unexplained. Mesalazine-associated myocarditis and ulcerative-colitis-associated inflammation remain alternatives, but unavailable medication timing and uncertain current disease activity prevent prioritizing them. A preceding respiratory illness supports, but does not prove, a postinfectious cause. Atrial biopsy and histology were unavailable, so neither myocarditis nor a specific inflammatory subtype is confirmed.

Cause and persistence of elevated pulmonary pressure and RV dysfunction
